title: Apply to 100 jobs in one night with ChatGPT
summary: Use ChatGPT's agent mode to find fresh roles on LinkedIn and Indeed, tailor your resume to each one and send applications while you watch the browser do the work.
cost: Paid ChatGPT plan (Plus or higher)
steps: Step 1: Map your resume to the right job titles
html:
✓What you need

  • A paid ChatGPT plan (Plus or higher). Agent mode is not available on the free plan.
  • A LinkedIn account and an Indeed account, both signed in.
  • Your current resume as a PDF or Word file.
  • 2 to 4 hours. The agent pauses for CAPTCHAs and custom questions, so stay close to your computer.

1Map your resume to the right job titles

This tells you which titles and keywords to target, so the agent does not waste applications on poor fits.

  1. Start a new chat in ChatGPT.
  2. Attach your resume.
  3. Send this prompt:
Prompt · Recruiter map
You are a senior recruiter. Read my resume and list the 20 job titles I am best qualified for. For each title, list the exact keywords and skills that applicant tracking systems (ATS) look for.
💡
If most jobs later score 0 for match, the titles were too broad. Run this prompt again and ask for narrower, more specific titles.

2Build one master resume

Stay in the same chat and send:

Prompt · Master resume
Rewrite my resume as a master version I can adapt to any role in seconds. Rewrite every bullet with Google's XYZ formula (Accomplished X, as measured by Y, by doing Z) and remove anything a hiring manager would reject at a glance.

What the XYZ formula does: every bullet becomes "achieved X, measured by Y, by doing Z". "Managed social media" turns into "Grew Instagram from 12K to 180K followers in 9 months by running a daily short-video pipeline". Recruiters skim a resume in about seven seconds, and bullets like this survive the skim.

What "remove what a hiring manager would reject" strips out:

  • Weak verbs: responsible for, involved in, helped with, worked on.
  • Buzzwords: synergy, ninja, rockstar, thought leader.
  • Claims with no number: "increased sales significantly" becomes "increased sales 34% quarter on quarter".
  • Paragraphs. Use bullets only, one or two lines each.

Save the result. Every tailored version in Step 4 starts from this file.

3Turn on agent mode

  1. In the same chat, click the + button below the message box.
  2. Switch on Agent mode (some accounts show it as ChatGPT agent).
  3. Allow it to open a browser if it asks.
  4. Sign in to LinkedIn and Indeed in your normal browser first.
💡
Tip: connect the Indeed app inside ChatGPT (Apps sidebar → Indeed → Connect). The agent can then read listings without leaving the chat, which avoids many CAPTCHAs.

4Search, score and apply

Send the search prompt:

Prompt · Search and score
Search LinkedIn and Indeed for every job posted in the last 7 days that matches my target titles from earlier. Build a spreadsheet with: job link, company, location, match score from 0 to 100, and a resume version tailored to that job. Put LinkedIn "Easy Apply" and Indeed "Apply now" jobs first. List any job that sends me to Workday, Greenhouse or Lever separately as a manual list.

A browser window opens that you can watch. The agent searches, filters by date, scores each job against your resume and fills the sheet. This takes 10 to 30 minutes.

Why Easy Apply first: one click with your resume pre-filled is where automation works best. Workday, Greenhouse and Lever need an account and custom answers, so keep those for a manual session.

When the sheet is ready, send:

Prompt · Auto-apply
Apply to the top 100 matches in the spreadsheet. For each one, use its tailored resume, answer short questions using the job description, and record the result in the sheet. If a cover letter is required, write one under 250 words that sounds like a real person, with no "I am writing to express my interest" opening.

A realistic run is 50 to 150 applications over 2 to 4 hours before it hits a rate limit or too many custom questions.

⚠️
The agent applies to real jobs using your real accounts. Watch the window and clear CAPTCHAs and questions when it pauses.
💡
Tell the agent to skip any job with more than three short-answer questions and log it to the manual list, so one long form does not stall the run.
💡
Some companies silently reject automated applications. Apply to those by hand.

5Raise your interview rate

💡
Tailoring beats volume. The same resume sent 100 times usually gets one or two interviews; a tailored resume per role sent 100 times gets far more (often eight to fifteen). The tailoring does the work, not the automation.
💡
Timing matters. Run it so applications land early in the recruiter's working morning in the target country, not at 3 AM. Applications read first get seen.

+Extra from Vaitis

  • Track replies: add columns for "Reply", "Interview date" and "Outcome" to the same sheet, and update them daily.
  • Quality check: before the auto-apply step, open five tailored resumes and read them. If anything is invented (a skill or number you do not have), tell the agent: "Never add skills, tools or numbers that are not in my master resume."
  • Follow up: five working days after applying, send a short, polite LinkedIn note to the recruiter for your top 10 roles.
  • Practise next: use the SkillNavora interview questions and practice tests to prepare for the calls you get.

title: Test your launch on an AI crowd with MiroFish
summary: MiroFish builds a crowd of AI personas, shows them your launch and reports how a market might react, so you can fix the price or message before going live.
time: About 1 hour for setup and a first run
cost: Free software; you pay your AI provider per use. Zep Cloud has a free monthly tier.
steps: Step 3: Fill in the settings file
Step 7: Read the report and ask follow-ups
html:
✓What you need

  • A Mac or Windows computer.
  • Node.js 18 or newer.
  • Python 3.11 or 3.12.
  • uv, the Python package manager.
  • An AI API key. The project suggests Alibaba's Qwen-plus through DashScope, but any OpenAI-compatible API works.
  • A Zep Cloud key, which gives the AI personas memory. The free monthly tier is enough to start.

1Download the code

Command · Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/666ghj/MiroFish.git
cd MiroFish

2Get your two keys

  • AI key: create an account with a provider and copy three things: the API key, its base URL and the model name. The default is Alibaba Bailian / DashScope with qwen-plus; OpenAI, or Gemini through a compatible proxy, also work.
  • Zep Cloud key: sign up free at getzep.com and copy the API key. The free monthly quota covers light use.

3Fill in the settings file

Copy the example file:

Command · Copy the settings file
cp .env.example .env

Open .env and add your values, one per line:

Command · Your .env values
LLM_API_KEY=your_api_key
LLM_BASE_URL=https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1
LLM_MODEL_NAME=qwen-plus
ZEP_API_KEY=your_zep_api_key
💡
Using another provider? Change LLM_BASE_URL and LLM_MODEL_NAME to that provider's values.
💡
Want it free? Point LLM_BASE_URL at your own FreeLLMAPI server (see the FreeLLMAPI guide in this library), which routes to free AI tiers through one OpenAI-compatible address.

4Install everything

One command installs the root project, the frontend and the backend:

Command · Install everything
npm run setup:all

Or install in stages:

Command · Install in stages
npm run setup
npm run setup:backend

5Start MiroFish

Command · Start MiroFish
npm run dev

Then open:

  • Dashboard (frontend): http://localhost:3000
  • Backend API: http://localhost:5001
💡
Run them separately with npm run backend and npm run frontend. With Docker, run docker compose up -d after Step 3 for the same ports.
💡
Fully local and free (no cloud AI bill): the community fork MiroFish-Offline swaps in Neo4j and Ollama. It needs a powerful computer, and local models are weaker than the big cloud models.

6Run your first simulation

  1. Upload your material: the launch post, landing-page text, new price, ad creative or a short product description. Research documents and background notes also work.
  2. Describe what you want to learn, in plain words. Example: "I'm launching a $49/month SaaS for indie founders. Test how they react to the price and the main headline. I worry it feels too expensive and too generic."
  3. Keep it small at first: a modest number of agents and under about 40 rounds, to control cost while you learn.
  4. Run it. MiroFish builds a knowledge graph from your material, creates AI personas with different backgrounds, lets them react and talk to each other, and tracks how opinions change.
💡
Use a cheaper, faster model while experimenting and save the best model for final runs. Watch your provider's usage page during the first few runs.

7Read the report and ask follow-ups

You get two things:

  • A prediction report: overall sentiment, the main objections, what worked and what fell flat.
  • A world you can explore: chat with any persona ("why did the price put you off?") and ask the Report Agent follow-up questions.

Fix the objections and framing problems it finds, then run again to compare.

8Know the limits

  • Simulated is not real. Treat results as ideas to test, not facts.
  • Quality in, quality out. Personas are only as good as your material and your question.
  • Realism costs money. Thousands of simulated customers are possible but expensive; most value comes from small, well-framed runs.
⚠️
MiroFish uses the AGPL-3.0 licence. Personal and internal use is fine; read the licence before building a commercial product on it.

+Extra from Vaitis

  • Confirm with real people: after the simulation, run a quick poll or a landing-page test with real visitors before you change your price.
  • Good questions to ask the crowd: "Which headline is clearer, A or B?", "What would stop you buying today?", "What price feels fair, and why?"
  • Save each run: keep the report and the exact input text, so you can compare versions over time.

title: Set up a free AI sales agent with Harvey
summary: Harvey is a free, open-source AI agent that finds leads, writes personal cold emails, sends them and follows up on replies, using the Claude plan you already pay for.
time: About 10 minutes to set up, plus 2 to 4 weeks of email warm-up
cost: Harvey is free. Needs a paid Claude plan (Pro or Max) and a paid Instantly plan (Growth or higher, for API access).
steps: Step 3: Tell Harvey what you sell
Step 4: Start Harvey and watch the pipeline
Extra from Vaitis: use Harvey for SkillNavora-style businesses
html:
✓What you need

  • A Mac or Windows computer.
  • A paid Claude plan (Pro or Max). Max is better if Harvey will run all day.
  • A paid Instantly plan to send the emails. Growth or higher includes the API access Harvey needs.
  • About 10 minutes.

1Install Claude Code

This is the only part you do by hand. After this, Claude does the setup for you.

On Mac:

  1. Open Terminal (press Cmd + Space, type Terminal, press Enter).
  2. Paste this line and press Enter:
Command · Install Claude Code (Mac)
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash

On Windows:

  1. Open PowerShell (press Start, type PowerShell, press Enter).
  2. Paste this line and press Enter:
Command · Install Claude Code (Windows)
irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex

Then on both:

  1. Close the terminal and open a new one.
  2. Type the command below and press Enter.
  3. A browser window opens. Sign in with the account that has your paid Claude plan.
Command · Start Claude Code
claude
💡
If Claude later asks to install Git or Python, say yes. Harvey needs them, and Claude can install them for you.

2Let Claude install Harvey

In the same Claude session, send this one message:

Prompt · Set up Harvey
Install Harvey for me from the start. Clone https://github.com/ethanplusai/harvey.git into a new folder, install everything it needs (including Python or Git if my computer is missing them), then run Harvey's setup wizard from start to finish. Train Harvey on my product using my website, connect my email tool and start it. Ask me for anything you need, and explain each step in simple words.

Follow along as Claude installs the parts and asks you a few questions.

💡
Harvey is a separate app that uses Claude as its brain, not a Claude plugin, so there is no /skills step. You confirm it works by opening its dashboard in Step 4.

3Tell Harvey what you sell

The setup wizard asks a few simple questions. This is the part that makes it work:

  • Your product: paste your website link. Harvey reads it and learns your product and ideal customer. No website? Type the answers instead.
  • Your ideal customer: the type of business you want (industry, size, location).
  • Your email tool: your Instantly API key, so Harvey can send. In Instantly: Settings → Integrations → API Keys.
⚠️
Skip the LinkedIn option. It can get your LinkedIn account restricted. Harvey finds leads from web search and company websites instead.
💡
Example: you build websites. You tell Harvey that, and it finds local businesses that fit, researches each one and writes a genuinely tailored email for each, not a template.
💡
401 error from Instantly? The API key is wrong or your plan has no API access. Create a new key under Settings → Integrations → API Keys.

4Start Harvey and watch the pipeline

When setup finishes, tell Claude "start Harvey", or run:

Command · Start Harvey
harvey run

Harvey now works in the background. It:

  • finds new leads that match your ideal customer,
  • researches each one,
  • writes a personal cold email for each,
  • sends them through Instantly,
  • reads replies and answers them to move towards a meeting,
  • repeats on the schedule you set.

Open the live dashboard in your browser:

Open in browser · Live dashboardOpen ↗
http://localhost:5555

The dashboard shows every lead, campaign and reply. To stop Harvey, go back to the terminal and press Ctrl + C. Nothing is sent while it is stopped.

💡
Harvey runs while your computer is on and the terminal is open. Running it all day and night on a server is possible later, but you don't need it to start.
💡
"command not found: harvey"? Tell Claude: "the harvey command isn't found, fix it".
💡
Not finding leads? Free web search gets rate-limited. Serper gives 2,500 free searches to start; its cheapest paid plan is $50 for 50,000 searches. Ask Claude to add a Serper API key.

5Protect your email reputation

Badly run cold email gets your address blocked. A few minutes here saves weeks of trouble.

  • Use a separate sending domain, not your main company email. Example: getyourbrand.com instead of yourbrand.com.
  • Turn on Instantly warm-up and leave it on for 2 to 4 weeks before real sending.
  • Start small: 10 to 20 emails a day, then increase slowly.
  • Always respect opt-outs. Harvey treats "stop" or "unsubscribe" as final. Keep it that way.
⚠️
This is not legal advice. For large volumes or regulated industries, speak to a lawyer first. In India, the EU and the US, cold email has rules (consent, identification, opt-out); follow them.
💡
Emails going to spam is almost always a domain problem, not your writing. Check your domain setup and warm-up, and halve your daily volume.

+Extra from Vaitis: use Harvey for SkillNavora-style businesses

  • Course or coaching business: ideal customer = "HR and L&D managers at 50 to 500 person companies in India". Offer a free workshop, not a sale, in the first email.
  • Measure it: track open rate, reply rate and meetings booked each week. A reply rate under 1% means the targeting or offer needs work.
  • Connect to your chatbot: send interested replies to your WhatsApp or Instagram bot (see the SkillNavora WhatsApp agent guide) so prospects get instant answers about fees and courses.

title: Build a hospital booking site that calls patients
summary: Build a hospital appointment website where every booking triggers an AI voice agent to call the patient and confirm, then saves the recording and details to one dashboard.
time: 30 to 45 minutes for a first version
cost: Phone number and per-minute calling cost in OmniDimension; Vercel, Supabase and Resend have free tiers.
steps: Step 2: Create the AI voice agent
Step 3: Connect the booking to the call and go live
Step 4: Set up Supabase and your dashboard
html:
✓What you need

  • A Mac or Windows computer with Claude Code installed (see the Harvey guide, Step 1).
  • An OmniDimension account for the AI voice agent, plus a phone number (buy one inside OmniDimension).
  • A Vercel account to put the site online.
  • A Supabase account to store bookings and call data.
  • A Resend account (or another email service) to email you the recording and details.
  • 30 to 45 minutes for a first version.
⚠️
Most steps are simple. The hard part is Step 3: the booking must start the call, and the call must report back. That is what turns a nice website into a working system, so go slowly there.

1Build the website

Open Claude Code in an empty folder and send:

Prompt · Build the site
Build a hospital appointment booking website with Next.js and Tailwind. Pages: Home, Doctors, Book Appointment, Contact. The booking form collects patient name, phone number, doctor, date, time and reason for visit. Style: clean, calm and medical, white with soft blue, modern and mobile-first. Keep it as one project I can deploy to Vercel.

Open the preview and keep asking for changes until it looks right:

Prompt · Refine the design
Make the hero section simpler with a bigger heading. Move the booking button to the top. Give the form rounded corners.

Then add your real details so it no longer looks like a demo:

Prompt · Add your real content
Replace all placeholder content with my real hospital.
Doctors: [name and specialty for each]
Services: [list]
Timings: [list]
Contact: [phone, email, address]
Use the logo and photos I have added to the project folder.
💡
Put your logo and photos in the project folder first, then tell Claude the file names.

2Create the AI voice agent

In OmniDimension, create a new Voice AI assistant. Choose a warm, natural voice and give it these instructions (change the hospital name):

Prompt · Voice agent instructions
You are the front-desk receptionist at [Hospital Name]. You are calling a patient to confirm the appointment they just booked. Be warm, clear and brief.
1. Greet the patient by name.
2. Confirm the doctor, date and time.
3. Ask whether the time still suits them.
4. If yes, confirm and thank them.
5. If no, say you will note a reschedule request and someone will call back.
Keep the call under one minute. Never give medical advice.

Then:

  • Buy a phone number in OmniDimension (or import a Twilio number) and attach it to this agent. This number calls patients.
  • Copy your API key and Agent ID. You need both in Step 3.
💡
Make a test call to your own phone before connecting anything. Fix the voice and script now, not later.

3Connect the booking to the call and go live

Back in Claude Code, send (add your Agent ID):

Prompt · Connect the booking
When someone submits the booking form, do three things on the server:
1. Save the booking to Supabase.
2. Call the OmniDimension API to start a confirmation call to the patient's phone, using Agent ID [your agent id].
3. Email me the booking details.
Read these from environment variables and never hard-code them: OMNIDIM_API_KEY, OMNIDIM_AGENT_ID, SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, RESEND_API_KEY, MY_EMAIL. Show me the .env file I need to fill in.

Deploy it. Add the Vercel plugin in Claude Code, then send:

Prompt · Deploy to Vercel
Add Vercel. Deploy this project to my Vercel account and give me the live link.

In Vercel, go to Project → Settings → Environment Variables, add your .env values and redeploy.

Close the loop: in OmniDimension, add a webhook that fires after each call and points to your live site, for example https://yoursite.com/api/call-result. Then in Claude Code:

Prompt · Receive the call result
Add an API route at /api/call-result that receives OmniDimension's webhook after each call. Save the recording link, transcript and outcome in Supabase against the matching booking, and email me the recording link with the patient details.

Now the loop runs on its own: a patient books, the AI calls within about a minute, and the result and recording reach Supabase and your inbox.

4Set up Supabase and your dashboard

Create a free Supabase project. In the SQL editor, create two tables:

SQL · Create the tables
create table bookings (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  name text,
  phone text,
  doctor text,
  appointment_date date,
  appointment_time text,
  reason text,
  status text default 'pending',
  created_at timestamptz default now()
);

create table call_logs (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  booking_id uuid references bookings(id),
  recording_url text,
  transcript text,
  outcome text,
  created_at timestamptz default now()
);

Copy the Project URL and anon key from Settings → API into your environment variables (same names as Step 3). Then add an admin page:

Prompt · Build the admin page
Add a password-protected admin page at /admin. Show a table of all bookings with their status and, for each, the linked call recording and outcome. Let me change a booking's status from this page.

Bookings, recordings and statuses now live in one place you can edit.

5Test before going live

Book a test appointment with your own number and check the whole loop: the call, the email and the dashboard.

⚠️
Calls cost money: you pay for the phone number and every minute. Start small and watch usage.
⚠️
Only call people who gave their number to book. Confirming their own appointment is fine; never use this to cold-call strangers.

+Extra from Vaitis

  • Patient data is sensitive. Turn on Row Level Security in Supabase, keep the admin page behind a strong password, and store only what you need. Follow your country's health-data rules (in India, the DPDP Act).
  • Reminders: ask Claude to add an SMS or WhatsApp reminder 24 hours before each appointment.
  • Same pattern, other businesses: salons, clinics, coaching centres and car service centres can use the same "book, then AI calls to confirm" flow.

title: Turn Claude into your Instagram manager with Ootto
summary: Connect Claude to Instagram through Ootto, send one prompt, and Claude studies your profile and plans a full week of Reels with hooks, scripts, captions and direction.
time: 5 minutes to connect, about 20 minutes per weekly plan
cost: Paid Claude plan (Pro or higher) for custom connectors; Ootto account
html:
✓What you need

  • A paid Claude plan (Pro or higher). Custom connectors are not on the free plan.
  • Your Instagram login, to connect the account through Ootto.
  • 5 minutes.
⚠️
Claude writes everything for your Reels and drafts it into Ootto. Animated graphics, voiceover audio and music arrive as direction (what to make and the mood), not finished files; you create those in your own tools. Whether Ootto posts automatically depends on your Ootto publishing setting.

1Connect Ootto to Claude

  1. In Claude, open Customize → Connectors.
  2. Click Add Custom Connector.
  3. Name it Ootto, paste the URL below into the URL field, and leave the advanced settings empty.
Open in browser · Connector URLOpen ↗
https://mcp.ootto.ai/mcp
  1. Click Add, then Connect, then Allow when Claude asks.
  2. A login screen opens. Sign in to Ootto, choose Instagram and click Allow access.

Ootto now shows in your connectors with an active status.

💡
No "Add Custom Connector" button? You are probably on the free plan; custom connectors need Pro or higher.
💡
Ootto won't connect? Check the URL is exactly https://mcp.ootto.ai/mcp and the advanced settings are empty. If the Instagram link fails, sign out of Ootto, sign back in and link Instagram again.

2Send the growth-manager prompt

Open a normal Claude chat and paste the whole prompt:

Prompt · Instagram growth manager
You are my Instagram growth manager, with access to my account through the Ootto connector. Work through these four stages in order, pause after each one to show me the result, and never publish anything without my approval.

STAGE 1: Study my account
Use Ootto to read my profile and my last 30 to 60 posts. Find: the Reels and posts with the most views, likes, saves and shares; the hooks and first lines that performed best; my average Reel length; my usual posting days and times; and the hashtags and topics in my best posts. Then tell me in plain words my niche, my audience and my top 3 content pillars (the themes that really perform).

STAGE 2: Find what works this week
Search the web for 8 to 10 trending topics, formats and angles in my niche this week. Keep only those that fit my pillars and audience.

STAGE 3: Plan 7 days of Reels
One Reel per day for the next 7 days. For each, give: the day and best posting time (from my own data); the on-screen title hook for the first frame; the first spoken line; the full script, word for word, in my voice; a ready-to-paste caption; 5 to 10 hashtags based on what works for me; visual direction scene by scene; voiceover tone and pace; and the type and mood of music. Write simply and like me, not like a generic influencer.

STAGE 4: Draft into Ootto
Save each Reel's caption and plan to my account as a draft or scheduled post. If Ootto can schedule, set them up but publish nothing until I say "go". If it cannot schedule, just give me everything so I can post myself.

Start with Stage 1 now.

3Approve each stage

Claude stops after each stage so you can check it:

  • After Stage 1: a plain-language read of your niche, audience and top 3 pillars.
  • After Stage 2: a shortlist of trending angles that fit your page.
  • After Stage 3: 7 complete Reels with hooks, scripts, captions, hashtags, posting times, and visual, voiceover and music direction.
  • After Stage 4: everything drafted in Ootto, waiting for your approval.

Nothing posts until you say go. Read each Reel, change anything that doesn't sound like you, then approve.

💡
It skipped straight to writing? Say: "Do Stage 1 first. Read my real posts through Ootto before writing anything."
💡
Sounds generic? Say: "Rewrite in my voice. Match the tone of my 3 best-performing Reels."
💡
Claude can't see your posts? Check Ootto shows as connected, then start a fresh chat.

4Repeat every week

Paste the same prompt each week. Claude re-reads your latest posts and plans a fresh week.

💡
If your Ootto account has scheduling on, ask Claude to spread the approved Reels across the week so they post on their own.

+Extra from Vaitis

  • For a course brand like SkillNavora: good pillars are "free learning tips", "student results (with permission)" and "behind the scenes of live classes".
  • Reply to DMs too: pair this with the SkillNavora Instagram auto-reply bot, so people who message after a Reel get instant answers.
  • Measure: after each week, ask Claude: "Compare last week's 7 Reels by views, saves and shares, and tell me what to repeat."

title: Let 7 AI advisors debate your business decision
summary: Roast Room is a free Claude skill that seats 7 AI advisors, each modelled on a well-known founder or investor's public work, to argue your decision, score the options and give you a PDF verdict.
time: 5 minutes to set up; 5 to 10 minutes per full council
cost: Free skill; runs on your paid Claude plan (Pro or higher), no API key
steps: Step 3: Install the Roast Room skill
Step 6: Watch the debate and get your verdict
html:
✓What you need

  • A Mac or Windows laptop.
  • A paid Claude plan (Pro or higher). Claude Code and the advisor sub-agents run on your plan; no API key needed.
  • Node.js 20 or newer (free).
  • 5 minutes.

1Install Claude Code

On Mac, open Terminal and paste:

Command · Install Claude Code (Mac)
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash

On Windows, open PowerShell and paste:

Command · Install Claude Code (Windows)
irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex

Then type claude, press Enter and sign in when asked.

💡
"claude: command not found"? Close and reopen the terminal, then try again.

2Install Node.js

Roast Room runs a small local app that shows the 7 advisors around a table, and that app needs Node. Download version 20 or newer from nodejs.org and install it with the default settings. Check it worked:

Command · Check Node
node --version

A number like v20.x means you are ready.

💡
"node: command not found"? Reinstall Node from nodejs.org and reopen the terminal.

3Install the Roast Room skill

Open Claude Code and send:

Prompt · Install Roast Room
Clone github.com/nateherkai/roast-room and set it up for me. Run git clone, go into the folder, check that the .claude/skills/roast-room folder exists, then run /skills so I can see all 7 advisor sub-agents loaded.
💡
Advisors missing from /skills? Say: "Reload the skills folder and run /skills again."

4Start the room

In your terminal, inside the roast-room folder, run:

Command · Start the room
npm start

Open this in your browser and keep the tab open. It is the live room where you watch the debate:

Open in browser · The roomOpen ↗
http://localhost:4730
💡
npm start fails? Make sure you are inside the folder first (cd roast-room). If the page won't load, check the npm start terminal is still running, then refresh.

5Run your first roast

Open Claude Code in the same folder (type claude) and send your decision:

Command · Run a roast
/roast-room [your decision here]

Give the council what it needs. Example:

Prompt · Example decision
/roast-room I run a D2C skincare brand making $40k a month with one full-time employee. Should I raise prices by 30%, launch a cheaper line, or spend the next 90 days only on content and keep prices flat? I have $25k in the bank. Success means $70k a month by March. I'm leaning towards the cheaper line because volume feels safer.

Always include: the decision, 2 or 3 options, your numbers (revenue, cash, team), your limits (deadline, budget), what success looks like and which way you lean. The Chair asks follow-up questions if something is missing.

⚠️
A full 7-advisor council uses real plan credit (21 sub-agent runs). For smaller questions use:
  • /roast-room --quick [decision]: 4 advisors, 2 rounds.
  • /roast-room --seats hormozi,buffett [decision]: only the advisors you choose.
  • /roast-room ask hormozi [question]: one answer from one seat.

6Watch the debate and get your verdict

Each advisor argues from one area of business:

Advisor seatFocusQuestion it asks
Jeff BezosStrategy and reversibilityIs this the right bet, and can you undo it?
Paul GrahamProduct-market fitDo people actually want it?
Alex HormoziOffer, pricing, salesWill people pay?
Gary VaynerchukAttention and marketingWhere will the eyeballs come from?
Dan MartellPeople, hiring, your calendarWho does this work?
Gino WickmanOperationsCan the business run without you?
Warren BuffettCash, risk, capitalWhat does this do to the money?

The advisors are AI personas based on these people's public writing and talks, not the people themselves. They score every option, weighted by how much their area matters to your decision, and the Chair limits the verdict if any seat flags a risk of ruin. You get a short verdict in Claude Code, a full report in the sessions folder and a one-click PDF in the room.

💡
Run another decision: open two terminals in the roast-room folder. In the first, run npm start to keep the room live. In the second, run claude, then /roast-room with the new decision. A full council takes 5 to 10 minutes.

+Extra from Vaitis

  • Treat it as a thinking partner, not an oracle. The verdict is only as good as the numbers you give it.
  • Good decisions to test: pricing changes, which course to launch next, hiring your first employee, or whether to run ads or grow organically.
  • Compare with the LLM Council guide in this library, which uses different models instead of personas.

title: Build a music streaming site with Claude Code
summary: Describe a Spotify-style music site to Claude Code and it builds the search, audio player and track art, then helps you fix bugs and put it online.
cost: Your Claude plan; hosting can be free (Netlify, Vercel, Cloudflare Pages)
steps: Step 1: Describe the whole site in one prompt
Step 2: Add your songs and images
Step 3: Show Claude the bug instead of describing it
html:
✓What you need

  • Claude Code installed and working (see the Harvey guide, Step 1).
  • A folder of songs you own or have permission to use (mp3 or similar).
  • A few background images for the tracks.
  • A rough idea of the look you want: colours, mood and layout.
⚠️
Use only music and images you have the rights to. If the site goes public, other people's songs or artwork can get it taken down.

1Describe the whole site in one prompt

Give Claude one clear, detailed prompt and let it build everything: structure, design, search and audio player. More detail now means fewer fixes later. A strong prompt covers:

  • What it is: "a smaller music streaming site like Spotify".
  • Main sections: home, search and a now-playing bar.
  • Player behaviour: play, pause, skip, progress bar and duration.
  • Look: dark theme, colours, font style.
  • Anything special: for example, songs grouped by place or mood.
Prompt · Example build prompt
Build a music streaming website like a smaller Spotify. Sections: a home page with playlists, a search page that filters songs as I type, and a now-playing bar fixed at the bottom. The player has play, pause, next, previous, a draggable progress bar and the track duration, and keeps playing while I move between pages. Dark theme with a green accent, rounded cards and a clean modern font. Group songs into playlists by mood. Use the songs and images in the /music and /images folders.
💡
Describe behaviour, not code. "The music keeps playing while I browse other pages" works better than naming a technical approach.

2Add your songs and images

Put your songs and images into the project, then send one instruction:

Prompt · Organise the media
Organise these songs and images and connect them to the player. Rename every file to a clean, consistent format, match each track with its background image, and read each song's real duration so the player shows the correct times.

Claude does the dull work: renaming files consistently, pairing each track with an image and reading real durations. You never label anything by hand.

3Show Claude the bug instead of describing it

When something breaks, don't try to explain it in words. Record your screen while using the broken part, then upload the recording to Claude. This works better because:

  • Claude sees the real behaviour: a broken layout, a missing image, a player that won't start.
  • You don't have to guess what the problem is called.
  • Claude can spot the cause and fix it directly.
💡
In the recording, do exactly the action that fails (click the button, load the page, press play) so the failure is on screen.

4Finish and publish

Ask Claude to finish the project:

Prompt · Finalise for hosting
Finalise the project for hosting: compress the images and audio so the site loads fast, delete unused files, and prepare everything for upload. Then give me step-by-step instructions to put it online for free, including which files to upload, where, and in what order.

Claude optimises the files, cleans the folder and prepares the build, then gives you exact publishing steps.

💡
The real lesson isn't the website: it's treating Claude like a developer who builds, tests, debugs and ships from start to finish.

+Extra from Vaitis

  • Free hosting options: Cloudflare Pages, Netlify and Vercel all host a static site like this for free.
  • Large audio files: many free hosts limit file size (Cloudflare Pages allows 25 MB per file). Ask Claude to convert songs to 128 to 192 kbps MP3 to stay under limits.
  • Next upgrades: liked songs saved in the browser, a shuffle button, and keyboard shortcuts (space to play or pause).

title: Set up JARVIS, your open-source voice assistant
summary: Install Claude Code, give it an open-source assistant project, add an ElevenLabs voice and your own tools, and get a voice assistant that reads your morning brief out loud.
cost: Paid Claude plan (Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise); ElevenLabs free tier (about 10,000 credits a month) to start
steps: Step 5: Run your first morning brief
html:
✓What you need

  • A computer running macOS 13+, Windows 10 (version 1809+) or Linux (Ubuntu 20.04+ / Debian 10+).
  • 4 GB of RAM or more and an internet connection.
  • A paid Claude plan (Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise). Claude Code is not on the free plan.
  • A GitHub account.
  • An ElevenLabs account. The free tier gives about 10,000 voice credits a month.
  • The GitHub link of the open-source assistant project you want to install.
⚠️
Wherever you see YOUR-REPO-URL below, use the real link of the assistant project you chose. The steps are the same for any open-source assistant project.

1Install Claude Code

Claude Code installs and runs everything else. Use the command for your system:

Command · Install Claude Code (macOS / Linux / WSL)
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash
Command · Install Claude Code (Windows PowerShell)
irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex
Command · Install Claude Code (any system with Node.js 18+)
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code

Check the installation:

Command · Check the install
claude --version
claude doctor

Start it. The first launch opens your browser to sign in:

Command · Start Claude Code
claude
💡
"command not found: claude"? Close and reopen the terminal (the installer updates your PATH). Still stuck? claude doctor tells you what is wrong.

2Give Claude the project

Create a folder for the assistant and open Claude Code inside it:

Command · Open Claude Code in a new folder
mkdir jarvis && cd jarvis
claude

Send this prompt (with your real link):

Prompt · Install the project
Clone this repository into the current folder, read its README, install all dependencies and get it running. Ask me for anything you need (API keys, settings) as you go: YOUR-REPO-URL

Claude downloads the files, installs dependencies and starts the project. When it needs something, such as a key, it stops and asks; reply in plain English.

💡
No project chosen yet? Search GitHub for open-source "Claude voice assistant" or "voice MCP" projects and use that link. The setup is the same.

3Add your ElevenLabs voice

This is what makes the assistant speak.

Get your API key:

  1. Sign in at elevenlabs.io.
  2. Open your profile → API Keys → create a new key.
  3. Copy it somewhere safe.

Choose a voice:

  1. Open Voices or the Voice Library.
  2. Preview a few and pick one.
  3. Copy its Voice ID.

Connect it. The simplest way is the official ElevenLabs MCP server. Install uv (a small helper), then add the server to Claude Code:

Command · Install uv and add ElevenLabs
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
claude mcp add elevenlabs --env ELEVENLABS_API_KEY=<your-key-here> -- uvx elevenlabs-mcp

Or, if your project uses a .mcp.json file, add this block with your key and voice ID:

Config · .mcp.json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "elevenlabs": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["elevenlabs-mcp"],
      "env": {
        "ELEVENLABS_API_KEY": "<your-key-here>",
        "ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID": "<your-voice-id>"
      }
    }
  }
}

Then test it:

Prompt · Test the voice
Use ElevenLabs for voice output with the voice ID I set. Say this out loud as a test: "Good morning, your assistant is online."

Restart Claude Code if it doesn't see the new server straight away.

⚠️
Each voice clip uses ElevenLabs credits. The free tier is enough for testing; heavy daily use may need a paid plan.

4Connect your tools

Link the assistant to what you use every day: calendar, inbox, dashboards, notes. Each tool connects as an MCP server, exactly like ElevenLabs. The pattern is always:

Command · Add a tool
claude mcp add <tool-name> --env KEY=value -- <command-that-starts-the-server>

See what is connected:

Command · List connected tools
claude mcp list

Then ask Claude to use the tools in your routine:

Prompt · Wire the tools in
I've connected my calendar and email. Update the assistant so my morning brief uses both: what's on my calendar today and which emails still need a reply.
💡
Google Calendar, Gmail, Notion and Slack all have ready-made MCP servers. Search "[tool name] MCP server" for the install command and add it with claude mcp add. Start with one or two tools.

5Run your first morning brief

Prompt · Morning brief
Give me my morning brief out loud: what's pending, what's important, and which emails I haven't answered yet.

Instead of scrolling through 40 emails you hear a short summary of what needs you. When you like the format, ask Claude to save it as a reusable command or a scheduled routine you can start with one word each morning.

💡
Being charged API rates on Pro or Max? An ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in your environment is overriding your subscription. Run unset ANTHROPIC_API_KEY to use your plan.
💡
MCP server not showing? Restart Claude Code and run claude mcp list. Install script returns 403? Usually a region, proxy or VPN issue: try another network or the npm method.

+Extra from Vaitis

  • Keep keys private: never paste API keys into a chat or commit them to GitHub. Keep them in .env or the MCP config on your own computer.
  • Useful routines: "evening wrap-up" (what got done, what moves to tomorrow), "meeting prep" (read the next meeting's invite and recent emails with that person).
  • Free voice option: for offline speech, ask Claude to add your computer's built-in text-to-speech as a fallback when ElevenLabs credits run out.

These skills never touch your YouTube account and never post anything. Claude writes, plans and checks; you upload.

The only manual step, done once.

Prompt · Install the YouTube Agent Skill
Install the YouTube Agent Skill for me from https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/youtube-agent-skill. I'm not technical, so do everything yourself and explain each step simply.

On a Mac, a pop-up may ask to install "command line developer tools". Click Install, wait, then tell Claude "done".

  1. Type /exit and press Enter.
  2. Type claude and press Enter.

You should see all 11: yt-script, yt-package, yt-edit, yt-comment, yt-plan, yt-viral, yt-retention, yt-shorts, yt-seo, yt-chapters, yt-audit.

Every skill reads one voice file. Set it up once and every script, title and reply sounds like you.

If you already have videos:

Prompt · Build my voice file from videos
Write my voice.md from these 3 videos and save it to ~/.claude/youtube/voice.md. Get the captions with yt-dlp; if that fails, tell me and I'll paste the scripts.
1. [LINK TO YOUR VIDEO]
2. [LINK TO YOUR VIDEO]
3. [LINK TO YOUR VIDEO]

If you have no videos yet:

Prompt · Build my voice file from an interview
Interview me one question at a time, then write my voice.md and save it to ~/.claude/youtube/voice.md.
💡
A better voice file gives better output. Redo it any time with your 3 best videos.

5Use the 11 skills

Type the command followed by your idea or file:

SkillWhat it doesTry
/yt-scriptTurns one idea into a full script with 5 scored hooks from 21 hook formulas/yt-script 5 free AI tools that replace a video editor
/yt-package10 title options plus a thumbnail idea for the best one/yt-package my video about free AI video editors
/yt-editWhere to cut (dead air, filler, retakes) with timecodesAttach your transcript (.srt), then /yt-edit
/yt-commentSorts comments, drafts replies in your voice, picks one to pinPaste comments, then /yt-comment
/yt-planPlans your week around the hours you really have/yt-plan I have 6 hours this week
/yt-viralFinds videos in your niche that beat their channel's average/yt-viral check these channels: [3 to 5 links]
/yt-retentionShows where viewers leave and whyAttach your YouTube Studio retention export, then /yt-retention
/yt-shortsFinds Shorts inside a long video and writes a new first line for eachAttach the transcript, then /yt-shorts
/yt-seoDescription, tags and 3 search terms to target/yt-seo my video about free AI video editors
/yt-chaptersChapters from your transcript that YouTube will displayAttach the transcript, then /yt-chapters
/yt-auditReviews the whole channel and gives you ONE fix/yt-audit my channel: [YOUR CHANNEL LINK]

From a viral idea to a finished package in one go:

Prompt · Viral idea to script to package
Use /yt-viral on these channels: [3 to 5 channel links in my niche]. Pick the best idea I could make this week. Then use /yt-script to write it in my voice, and /yt-package to give me titles and a thumbnail idea.
💡
Thumbnails come as a written brief (expression, framing, 3 words, background); you or a designer make the image. /yt-edit gives a cut list; you or an editor do the cutting.
💡
Hook scores are a guide, not a promise. If a skill needs a number it doesn't have, it asks you instead of inventing one.
💡
For transcript skills, download an .srt from YouTube Studio → Subtitles or any transcription tool.

+Extra from Vaitis

  • Weekly rhythm: Monday /yt-plan, Tuesday /yt-viral + /yt-script, after filming /yt-edit, before upload /yt-package + /yt-seo + /yt-chapters, 48 hours after upload /yt-comment, monthly /yt-audit.

cd gods-eye-view
npm ci
npm run dev

3Open the live map

Open in browser · The mapOpen ↗
http://localhost:4173

Layer groupWhat you see
AirLive flights and military aircraft
SeaShips and submarine cables

Command · Install Claude Code (Mac)
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash

Windows (PowerShell):

Command · Install Claude Code (Windows)
irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex

Type claude, press Enter and sign in.

💡
"command not found"? Close and reopen the terminal and try again.

2Install the Arena skill

In Claude Code, send this with the Arena repository link:

Prompt · Install Arena
Install the Arena skill from this GitHub repository: [paste the repository link]. Clone it, install it as a Claude skill with any dependencies it needs, then run /skills to confirm it is loaded.

When it finishes, /skills lists Arena.

💡
Clone fails? Send: "Retry the Arena install and show me the exact error if it fails." Not in /skills? Send: "Reload the skills folder and run /skills again."

3Run Arena on a prompt

Prompt · Run Arena
Use the Arena skill on this prompt: [your prompt: a coding problem, a piece of writing, a strategy question or a design decision, ideally one where your first attempt wasn't sharp enough]

4Watch the 100 agents compete

  1. Arena starts 100 small Claude agents, each with the same prompt.
  2. Each answers in its own way, with different reasoning, structure and angle.
  3. They review each other's answers and point out mistakes.
  4. Weaker answers are eliminated round by round.
  5. One winner survives, and that's what you see.

You watch the rounds in the terminal. The final answer comes with a short note on why it won.

5Know when to use it

Arena uses far more credit than a normal run (100 agents instead of 1). Save it for when:

  • the first answer was clearly wrong,
  • the task is open-ended and the best answer isn't obvious,
  • you're about to ship, publish or send something important,
  • you've re-prompted 2 or 3 times and keep getting similar, average answers.

For simple questions, a normal Claude chat is enough.

⚠️
Because it runs 100 agents at once, Arena uses a lot of your plan credit. Use fewer agents for smaller jobs: "Run Arena on this prompt with 20 agents instead of 100: [your prompt]".
💡
To use it again later, open Claude Code and send: "Use the Arena skill on this: [your prompt]".

+Extra from Vaitis

  • Great uses for learners: the strongest answer to a tough interview question, a sharper resume summary, or the best structure for a PRD.
  • Free alternative to try first: ask one Claude chat for "5 very different answers, then critique each and combine the best parts". It's cheaper and often good enough.

title: Scrape any site into a dashboard with Claude
summary: Connect Claude to Apify, paste a URL, and Claude picks a scraper, tests it, runs it and turns the data into a searchable dashboard you can filter and export.
