steps: Step 1: Connect Claude to Apify (one time)
Step 2: Send the URL with this prompt
Step 6: Turn it into a paid service (optional)
html:
✓What you need

  • A paid Claude plan (Pro or higher). Connectors aren't on the free plan.
  • An Apify account. The free plan includes $5 of usage credit each month.
  • The URL of the website you want data from.
  • About 10 minutes.

1Connect Claude to Apify (one time)

  1. Open Claude on desktop or web.
  2. Go to Settings → Connectors.
  3. Search Apify and click Connect.
  4. Sign in to Apify in the tab that opens and click Authorize.
  5. Back in Claude, Apify shows as an active connector.

Claude can now run Apify scrapers (called "Actors") for you.

2Send the URL with this prompt

Open a new chat:

Prompt · Scrape a site
I want data from this website: [PASTE URL]. First ask me what data I need. Then: 1) choose the best Apify Actor for the job, 2) configure it, 3) run a small test of 5 to 10 items, 4) show me a sample of the results, 5) if it looks right, run the full scrape, 6) save the results as a clean dataset. Show me readable data, not raw JSON.

3Answer Claude's questions

Claude asks two or three things in plain English; no settings files or code. For a Shopify store it might ask:

  • Which fields: product name, price, images, description, stock?
  • How many products: all, or the top 100?
  • Any particular category?

4Check the test run

Claude first scrapes 5 to 10 items, which protects your Apify credit if something is wrong. You see a preview of the fields, such as name, price, image link and stock.

If it looks right, say "run the full scrape". If a field is missing, say so, for example "also get the review count".

5Get your dashboard

Prompt · Build a dashboard
Build me a searchable dashboard for this data with a search bar, filters for category and price, sorting by any column, and export to CSV.

Claude builds it as an artifact. You can search any item, filter by any scraped field and download everything as CSV or Excel.

6Turn it into a paid service (optional)

The same scrape-and-dashboard can be sold:

ClientWhat they'd pay for
E-commerce brandCompetitor pricing dashboard, updated weekly
Real estate agentEvery new listing in their city, filterable
Local businessDirectory of competitors and their offers
D2C founderAmazon reviews of competitor products
RecruiterEvery job posting from target companies

A typical starting price is $200 to $500 for a one-time scrape and dashboard, plus $50 to $150 a month for weekly refreshes.

⚠️
Don't scrape sites that forbid it. Check the site's robots.txt and terms. Public product pages are usually fine; LinkedIn and Facebook are off-limits. Never collect personal data without a lawful reason.
💡
Don't run huge scrapes on the free tier; the $5 credit goes quickly. Upgrade before a paid client project.
💡
Always test one page first, even on a site you've scraped before, because pages change. Save the exact prompt you used: the same prompt on the same site gives a repeatable delivery.

+Extra from Vaitis

  • Job-search use: scrape public job boards for "AI product manager" roles in your city and build a dashboard sorted by posting date.
  • Schedule refreshes: Apify can run an Actor on a schedule (weekly) so the client's dashboard stays current.
  • Freelance tie-in: see SkillNavora's Master Freelancing page to package this as a service with a clear scope and price.

title: Turn Claude Code into a senior UI engineer
summary: Three free Claude skills plus two MCP servers give Claude Code real design taste, let it design in Figma, build the site and test it in a real browser. Installs in about 10 minutes.
cost: Free skills and servers; Claude plan; Figma Dev or Full seat for the Figma MCP
steps: Step 1: Install the Emil Kowalski skill
Step 4: Set up the Figma MCP server
Step 5: Install the Playwright MCP server
html:
✓What you need

  • Claude Code installed and signed in.
  • Node.js 18 or newer.
  • The Figma desktop app (the web version won't work for the Figma MCP) and a Figma Dev or Full seat.
  • Any project folder to try the setup in.

The five parts: three skills (Emil Kowalski, Impeccable and Taste) are the design brain; two MCP servers (Figma and Playwright) are the hands and eyes.

1Install the Emil Kowalski skill

This covers animation craft, easing and the small details that make an interface feel right.

Command · Install the Emil skill
npx skills add emilkowalski/skills --agent claude-code

It adds six sub-skills to .claude/skills/ in the current project:

  • emil-design-eng: the main skill (UI polish, animation decisions, component design).
  • review-animations: checks your animations against Emil's rules.
  • improve-animations: returns a prioritised list of fixes.
  • find-animation-opportunities: shows where motion helps and where it hurts.
  • prototype: builds several genuinely different versions of a UI element.
  • A design-review skill focused on design decisions.

They trigger automatically when you ask Claude to build, review or improve UI. To check, ask Claude "What skills do you have available?"

2Install the Impeccable skill

Impeccable adds about 20 slash commands for typography, colour contrast, spacing and interaction states. Inside Claude Code run:

Command · Install Impeccable
/plugin marketplace add pbakaus/impeccable
/plugin install impeccable@impeccable

The one you'll use most is /polish: a full clean-up pass on the current file covering typography, contrast, spacing, interaction states, focus rings and dialog behaviour. It's the fastest way to stop an AI-built page looking AI-built.

3Install the Taste skill

Taste blocks generic AI design and draws on a curated set of well-designed sites. Choose one:

Option A: the standalone community version (strictest about avoiding generic output, most widely used):

Command · Install Taste (option A)
npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill --skill "design-taste-frontend"

Option B: a merged skill combining Emil, Impeccable and Taste without duplicates. Useful if the three separate skills overlap for you:

Command · Install Taste (option B)
npx skills add h3nryprod01/design-taste

4Set up the Figma MCP server

Install the official plugin:

Command · Install the Figma plugin
claude plugin install figma@claude-plugins-official

Restart Claude Code, run /plugin, open the Installed tab, select figma, press Enter and finish the sign-in in the browser.

Then switch on Figma's server:

  1. Open the Figma desktop app.
  2. Open a Figma Design file.
  3. With nothing selected, switch to Dev Mode.
  4. In the right sidebar, enable MCP Server.
  5. You'll see a confirmation that it's running.

Test it by selecting a frame in Figma and sending:

Prompt · Convert a Figma frame
Convert my current Figma selection into a React component with Tailwind CSS.

5Install the Playwright MCP server

Playwright lets Claude open your site in a real browser, take screenshots and check its own work.

Command · Add Playwright MCP
claude mcp add playwright --scope user -- npx -y @playwright/mcp@latest

Or add it to ~/.claude.json (or a project .mcp.json):

Config · Playwright in .mcp.json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "playwright": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@playwright/mcp@latest"]
    }
  }
}

Restart Claude Code. The first run downloads Chromium (about 200 MB, once). Run /mcp and check playwright is connected. Test:

Prompt · Screenshot and check a page
Open my dev server at localhost:3000, take a screenshot and tell me whether the hero section looks broken.

6Use the whole stack

One prompt now runs the full loop:

Prompt · Build a landing page
Build a landing page for a fintech SaaS called "Vault": modern and minimal, with a strong hero, three feature cards, three pricing tiers and a footer. Use Next.js, Tailwind and shadcn/ui.

Behind the scenes: Taste reads the brief and sets a real design direction, Emil decides what should move and with which easing, Impeccable enforces typography, contrast, spacing and states, Claude writes the code within those rules, and Playwright opens the page at mobile, tablet and desktop sizes and flags anything broken. Claude keeps fixing until Playwright confirms it works.

With a Figma design ready:

Prompt · Figma to production code
Convert the design in my selected Figma frame into production code, matching it pixel for pixel. Test it in the browser when done.

+Extra from Vaitis

  • Check accessibility too: ask "Run an accessibility check with Playwright: contrast, focus order and labels."
  • Phone first: always ask Playwright to test at 390 px wide; most of your visitors are on phones.
  • Portfolio idea: rebuild one of your own old projects with this stack and show the before and after.

title: Run your resume past a 7-Claude hiring panel
summary: Paste your resume and a target job description, and a 7-reviewer panel inside Claude, from the ATS to a sceptic, judges you independently, then rewrites your resume with every weakness fixed.
cost: Works on the free Claude plan; longer resumes may need a paid plan
steps: Step 2: Fill in and send the panel prompt
html:
✓What you need

  • Your current resume (copied text or the file).
  • The full job description of the role you really want.
  • A Claude chat at claude.ai.
💡
Always give the panel a real job description. A resume isn't good or bad on its own; it's good for a specific role, and the panel is much sharper with a target.

1Open a fresh chat

Start a new conversation so nothing earlier affects the review.

2Fill in and send the panel prompt

Paste the prompt below, replace the two placeholders with your real text, then send. The seven reviewers judge you independently and only meet in the final summary.

Prompt · The 7-person hiring panel
Run my resume through a 7-person hiring panel for one specific job.

Rules: each reviewer works independently and does not see the others' verdicts; each judges my resume only against the job description below; be blunt and specific; every point must refer to something actually in my resume, with no generic advice.

For each reviewer give: VERDICT (PASS, BORDERLINE or REJECT), SCORE out of 10, the TOP 3 reasons specific to my resume, and the ONE fix that would most change their mind.

The reviewers:
1. The ATS (automated screener): keyword match, required qualifications, clean formatting. Would it reach a human at all?
2. The recruiter: an 8-second skim for fit, gaps, red flags and level.
3. The hiring manager: interview yes or no, judging impact, relevance to this role and proof over claims.
4. A rival applicant: where would a similar candidate beat me?
5. The CEO: the business case, including outcomes, ownership, leadership and return on investment.
6. A future teammate: would I want to work with this person? Clarity, collaboration, trust.
7. The sceptic: vague claims, buzzwords, unverifiable numbers and filler.

After all 7: A) PANEL SUMMARY with the overall verdict, my average score and the 3 problems most reviewers raised. B) THE REWRITE: a complete improved resume with every issue fixed, stronger bullets, real metrics where I have them (ask me if you need numbers), tighter wording and ATS-friendly formatting. Keep it truthful: never invent experience, titles or results.

=== JOB DESCRIPTION ===
[PASTE THE JOB DESCRIPTION HERE]

=== MY RESUME ===
[PASTE YOUR RESUME HERE]

3Read the panel report

You get a verdict, score and single biggest fix from each reviewer, then a combined summary.

💡
Fix the problems several reviewers share first. If 5 of 7 flag the same weakness, that's your most valuable edit.

4Use the rewritten resume

The prompt ends with a full rewrite that addresses every issue.

💡
Be honest with Claude: the rewrite is only as truthful as your input. Never let it invent titles or results. Real numbers win: "Grew revenue 40%" beats "responsible for growth" with every reviewer.

5Go further (optional)

Use these one at a time after the first report.

Prompt · Go deeper on one reviewer
Reviewer 3 (the hiring manager) rejected me. Go through my resume line by line as that person and show me how to rewrite each weak bullet.
Prompt · Add real metrics
Here are real numbers from my last job: [details]. Rework my bullets to use them, and flag any claim that still sounds vague.
Prompt · Tailor to a second job
Here's a different job description: [paste]. Re-run only the ATS and the hiring manager, and tell me what to change so the same resume fits this role.
Prompt · Final polish
Give me the final resume as clean, copy-ready text with consistent formatting, strong action verbs and no buzzwords. Then list 5 things I should still check myself.
💡
Run the panel for each job, not once. The same resume scores differently for different roles.

+Extra from Vaitis

  • For product roles: add an 8th reviewer: "A senior product manager judging product sense: problems solved, metrics moved and trade-offs made."
  • Interview prep next: ask "Based on the hiring manager's concerns, give me the 10 interview questions I'm most likely to get and model answers using my real experience."
  • Combine with guide 001: use the panel's rewrite as the master resume for the 100-applications run.

title: Turn messy ideas into pro prompts with Prompt Master
summary: Prompt Master is a free Claude skill that turns a messy one-line idea into a complete, professional prompt for any AI tool, detecting the target tool and fixing patterns that waste tokens.
cost: Free; works with a Claude.ai account or Claude Code
steps: Step 2: Use it in four ways
Extra from Vaitis: the 6-part prompt checklist
html:
✓What you need

  • A Claude.ai account, or Claude Code installed.
  • About 60 seconds. No Python, Node or API keys.

1Install Prompt Master

Choose where you want it.

Path A: claude.ai (simplest)

  1. Open the repository (link above).
  2. Click the green Code button, then Download ZIP.
  3. Open claude.ai.
  4. In the sidebar go to Customize → Skills.
  5. Click Upload and drop in the ZIP.
  6. Prompt Master now works in every chat.

Path B: Claude Code (for developers). Clone it into your global skills folder:

Command · Install into Claude Code (all projects)
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills
git clone https://github.com/nidhinjs/prompt-master.git ~/.claude/skills/prompt-master

Restart Claude Code. For a single project only, clone it inside that project instead:

Command · Install into one project
git clone https://github.com/nidhinjs/prompt-master.git .claude/skills/prompt-master

Path C: Cursor. Same idea, different folder:

Command · Install into Cursor
git clone https://github.com/nidhinjs/prompt-master.git ~/.cursor/skills/prompt-master
⚠️
Do not put it in ~/.cursor/skills-cursor/. That folder is reserved for Cursor's built-in skills, and third-party skills there break things.

2Use it in four ways

All four use the same engine but enter different modes.

1. Natural language (most common). Just describe what you want:

Prompt · Natural language
Turn this into a proper prompt: I want Claude to build a landing page for my dog grooming business

Prompt Master detects the target tool, chooses a structure, spots missing details (no colours, sections or tech stack) and returns a finished prompt.

2. Explicit call, for tighter control when the target isn't obvious:

Prompt · Explicit call
/prompt-master
Target: Midjourney
Task: A cinematic hero shot of my product

3. Decompiler mode, to find what's wrong with an existing prompt:

Prompt · Decompile a prompt
Decompile this prompt and tell me what's wrong with it: "Write me a blog post about AI. Make it engaging."

It names the problems and returns a rewritten version with the fixes explained.

4. Cross-tool translation, to move a prompt between tools:

Prompt · Translate across tools
Translate this Midjourney prompt for Sora: "cinematic wide shot, golden hour, 35mm anamorphic, shallow depth of field"
💡
Example result: "help me build the landing page for my SaaS, it's like Linear but for lawyers" comes back as a full prompt with context, goal, style, tone, audience, tech stack, section order, file structure and a clear "stop when" condition, so the AI never needs to ask a follow-up question.

+Extra from Vaitis: the 6-part prompt checklist

Even without the skill, a strong prompt includes:

  1. Role: who the AI should act as.
  2. Goal: the single outcome you want.
  3. Context: audience, background, constraints.
  4. Inputs: the data or text to use.
  5. Format: length, structure, tone, file type.
  6. Done when: how the AI knows it has finished.

Learn more in SkillNavora's free Prompt and Context Engineering PDF.

title: Build a live data dashboard from a folder in Claude
summary: Point Claude at a folder of spreadsheets or a connected app and it builds an interactive dashboard that re-reads your data, chooses the charts and answers plain-English questions about the numbers.
cost: Paid Claude plan (Pro is $20 a month, or $17 a month billed yearly); not on the free plan
steps: Step 2: Ask Claude to build the dashboard
html:
✓What you need

  • A paid Claude plan (Pro or higher).
  • Claude on web, desktop or mobile. Reading a local folder needs the desktop app; a connected source (Google Drive, Notion and so on) works anywhere.
  • A data source: a local folder of CSV, XLSX or JSON files, or a connected app (Google Drive, Notion, Airtable, Slack or a custom MCP server).
💡
There is nothing separate to install; the dashboard is an artifact Claude builds for you.

1Prepare your data

Local folder: create a folder (for example company-data) and put your files in it, such as sales-2026-q3.csv, customer-list.csv and product-inventory.xlsx. Claude reads CSV, XLSX, JSON, plain text and Markdown.

Connected app (best for a dashboard a team keeps using):

  1. In Claude, open the sidebar and go to Connectors.
  2. Turn on the connector for your source (Google Drive, Notion, etc.).
  3. Finish signing in. The dashboard now reflects the source whenever it changes.

2Ask Claude to build the dashboard

Start a new chat:

Prompt · Build the dashboard
Build me an interactive dashboard artifact from the folder ~/Desktop/company-data. Read all CSV and XLSX files in it and choose the most useful chart types for the columns. Include a Refresh button that re-reads the data and updates every chart, a chat box at the bottom that answers questions like "which region performed best this quarter?", and a "last refreshed" time. Design: clean, professional and minimal, with colours that work in light and dark mode. Layout: KPI cards at the top, charts in the middle, the chat box at the bottom, and the raw-data table collapsed by default.

Using a connected app? Change the first sentence, for example: "Build me an interactive dashboard artifact from my Google Drive folder called Company Data, using the Google Drive connector." Keep the rest.

Claude reads the data (or calls the connector), chooses the charts and adds the dashboard to your Artifacts.

3Open and refresh it

Open the artifact from your Artifacts view. It re-reads the folder or connector so you see current data. The chat box runs as whoever is using it, so each person needs their own Claude access to ask questions.

4Share it (Team or Enterprise)

On Team or Enterprise plans you can share it inside your organisation. People who open it sign in to the same organisation and it uses their own connectors and data. On Pro, the dashboard stays private to your account.

+Extra from Vaitis

  • Clean data first: consistent column names and one header row make charts far more accurate. Ask: "List any columns with missing or inconsistent values before building."
  • Good starter KPIs: total revenue, number of customers, average order value, growth versus last period.
  • Practise the skill: SkillNavora's free Excel, SQL and Power BI lessons teach the same thinking behind good dashboards.

title: Run your decision past a 5-advisor LLM Council
summary: LLM Council is a free Claude Code skill that puts your question to five independent advisors, from a contrarian to an executor, has them peer-review each other anonymously, and ends with one chairman's verdict.
time: 2 minutes to install; 4 to 6 minutes per council
cost: Free skill; paid Claude plan (Pro or higher)
html:
✓What you need

  • A paid Claude plan (Pro or higher). Claude Code isn't on the free plan.
  • Claude Code installed and signed in, or Claude on claude.ai.
  • Nothing else: no API keys, MCP servers or scripts. It's a pure skill that runs on sub-agents.

1Install LLM Council

Path A: let Claude install it (easiest). In Claude Code or claude.ai, send:

Prompt · Install LLM Council
Please install this Claude skill. The SKILL.md file is at https://github.com/oliwoodman/llm-council-skill. Set it up as a global skill so I can use it in any project, and walk me through anything you need from me.

Claude fetches the file, creates ~/.claude/skills/llm-council/ and confirms it's ready. Restart Claude Code once.

Path B: clone it yourself:

Command · Install with git
git clone https://github.com/oliwoodman/llm-council-skill ~/.claude/skills/llm-council

Path C: one command, no git (a fork with the same advisor structure):

Command · Install with skill add
claude skill add --url https://raw.githubusercontent.com/automatorsplus/llm-council-skill/main/.claude/skills/llm-council/SKILL.md

2Call a council

Start your message with the trigger phrase, then your question:

Prompt · Run a council
council this: [your question or decision]

Examples:

  • council this: should I quit my job to build my SaaS full-time?
  • council this: my agency makes $10k a month. Should I hire my first employee or stay solo?
  • council this: should I raise my consulting rate from $50 to $100 an hour? Will I lose more clients than I gain?
  • pressure-test this: I want to launch a paid founders' community at $29 a month. Here's my plan: [describe it]

Claude runs the five advisors in parallel, then an anonymous peer review, then the chairman's verdict. A full council takes about 4 to 6 minutes.

3Understand the verdict

Each advisor answers first through one lens:

AdvisorLens
The ContrarianHunts for the fatal flaw: what's missing and what will fail. Doesn't hedge.
The First-Principles ThinkerAsks whether you're solving the right problem and reframes it from scratch.
The ExpansionistLooks for the upside others missed, ignoring risk (that's the Contrarian's job).
The OutsiderKnows nothing about you or your field and reacts only to what's in front of it.
The ExecutorOnly cares what you do first: "what happens on Monday morning?"

Next, all five grade each other anonymously, without knowing who wrote what, which keeps the review honest rather than defensive. Finally the Chairman commits to one verdict in about 250 words: the call (go, don't or conditional), the strongest reason, the biggest risk and a next step within 7 days. If Claude starts to hedge, the skill forces it to commit.

💡
The Outsider is the most underrated advisor. Run council this: [your product description] and it tells you what a first-time visitor won't understand, the way a stranger reads your landing page. That's often worth more than the other four together.
💡
Want different AI models instead of one? This skill uses five Claude sub-agents with different lenses. Andrej Karpathy's original LLM Council makes Claude, GPT, Gemini and Grok argue and review each other. It's a local web app, takes about 15 minutes to set up and needs an OpenRouter API key with roughly $5 to $10 of credit.

+Extra from Vaitis

  • Give it numbers: revenue, savings, time available and deadline. Councils with real numbers give much sharper verdicts.
  • Career decisions work too: "council this: should I switch from business analyst to product manager in the next 6 months?"
  • Then act: turn the Chairman's 7-day next step into a calendar task straight away.

title: Make any photo move like you with Wan AI
summary: Wan AI's Animate tool copies your expressions and movements from a video you record onto the character in a photo, and renders it as an HD video in your browser, free to try.
cost: Free credits on sign-up (enough for a few tests); more credits for 1080p and extra runs
steps: Step 4: Record and upload your movement video
Step 5: Choose output settings and generate
html:
✓What you need

  • A wan.video account (sign in with Google or email; no app or download).
  • A clear, front-facing photo of the character you want to animate.
  • A short video of yourself, 5 to 15 seconds, doing the movement you want.
  • A browser. Free credits are added at sign-up, enough to test a few times.
⚠️
Only animate photos you have the right to use, and never use this to impersonate a real person. Putting someone's face on your movements without consent can cause real harm, and in many countries it is illegal.

1Sign in

  1. Open wan.video.
  2. Click Sign in (top right).
  3. Use Google or email.

2Open Wan Animate

  1. On the home page, click Create (or Generate) in the top menu.
  2. In the sidebar, find Video → Wan Animate (sometimes called Animate or Move).
  3. Click it. You'll see two upload slots: one for the image, one for the video.

3Upload the reference photo

This is the character that will move.

Works best: a clear, front-facing photo with the whole face visible, no heavy shadows, head-and-shoulders or half-body, one person only.

Avoid: side profiles; faces covered by hands, sunglasses or masks; more than one person; low-resolution or blurry images.

Click the Image slot, drag in your photo and wait for the preview.

4Record and upload your movement video

Wan copies the motion from this clip.

  • Frame yourself from the chest or waist up (the more of you is visible, the more motion it can transfer).
  • Face the camera directly, with even lighting and a plain background.
  • Keep it to 5 to 15 seconds.
  • Do exactly what the character should do: talk, laugh, wave, gesture.

Record on your phone and upload it (or record inside Wan if offered). Click the Video slot, upload the clip and wait a few seconds.

5Choose output settings and generate

Check the side panel:

SettingChoice
Resolution720p or 1080p (1080p costs more credits but looks better on social media)
Aspect ratio9:16 for Reels and Shorts, 16:9 for YouTube, 1:1 for square posts
DurationMatches your video by default
Mode"Animate" or "Motion Transfer", not "Replace" or "Relight" unless you want those

Click Generate. A short clip usually takes 1 to 3 minutes. Keep the tab open and watch the progress bar.

6Review and download

The preview plays automatically. Check three things:

  1. The character still looks like the reference photo.
  2. The movements match your video.
  3. There's no strange warping around the hands or edges.

If it looks good, click Download to save the MP4. If not, improve the photo or video (better lighting, plainer background, simpler movement) and try again.

💡
The first try is rarely perfect; allow 2 to 3 generations. Simpler movement gives cleaner results; keeping your hands away from your face avoids the most common finger glitches; and a character with body proportions similar to yours avoids stretching.
💡
Record your movement once and apply it to several photos to keep one character consistent across a series.

+Extra from Vaitis

  • Ideas for a course brand: an animated mascot that introduces each lesson, or a "tip of the day" character for Reels.
  • Label AI content: add "AI-generated" to the caption. Instagram and YouTube ask creators to disclose realistic AI media.

title: Keep Claude Code running past its limits with 9Router
summary: 9Router is a free local proxy between your coding tool and 40+ AI providers. When your Claude plan hits its limit, it switches to a cheap or free backup mid-session so you keep working.
cost: Free software; optional cheap providers (about $0.20 to $0.60 per million tokens) and free fallbacks
steps: Step 6: Turn on RTK Token Saver
Step 8: Use it with other tools (optional)
html:
✓What you need

  • Node.js 18 or newer, and npm.
  • Claude Code, or any coding tool with a custom endpoint setting.
  • A browser for the dashboard.
  • Ideally an existing Claude plan (especially Max). 9Router works best as the backup behind it.

1Install and start 9Router

Command · Install 9Router
npm install -g 9router
Command · Start 9Router
9router

It prints a dashboard address and an API endpoint, both on port 20128.

Prefer a guided 5-minute setup that walks you through providers? Use the starter kit:

Command · Starter kit (optional)
git clone https://github.com/aiflowlearn/9router-starter-kit
cd 9router-starter-kit
./install.sh
./configure.sh

2Open the dashboard

Open in browser · DashboardOpen ↗
http://localhost:20128

You land on the Providers page with nothing connected.

3Connect 2 or 3 providers

Click Providers and choose. A good starter set across three tiers:

TierProviderCostHow to connect
1. Your subscriptionClaude CodeYour planClick Connect and sign in. 9Router tracks your 5-hour and weekly limits live.
2. Cheap paid backupGLM (Z.ai)About $0.60 per 1M tokensSign up at z.ai, create an API key, paste it
2. Cheap paid backupMiniMaxAbout $0.20 per 1M tokensSign up at minimax.io, create a key, paste it
3. Free fallbackiFlowFree (Kimi K2 Thinking)Browser sign-in
3. Free fallbackQwenFree (Qwen models)Browser sign-in
3. Free fallbackKiroFree (Claude 4.5, GLM-5, MiniMax)AWS Builder ID, Google or GitHub sign-in

Each free connection is one browser click with no credit card. Providers set their own prices and can change them, so check their sites.

⚠️
Don't add Gemini CLI to this chain for use in other tools. Google's terms limit free Gemini CLI tokens to Gemini CLI itself; routing them into Claude Code may get your account banned. The dashboard flags this next to Gemini CLI.

4Build your fallback chain

In the dashboard, open Combos → Create Combo. A solid order for Claude Code users:

  1. Your Claude Code subscription (used fully first).
  2. A cheap backup when the limit runs out, such as GLM 5.2.
  3. A free emergency fallback, such as Kimi K2 Thinking via iFlow.

Save it. Your plan does the heavy work, a few dollars of cheap overflow fills gaps, and free tiers catch the rest.

5Point Claude Code at 9Router

Create a key in the dashboard under Settings → API Keys, then in your terminal:

Command · Route Claude Code through 9Router
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="http://localhost:20128/v1"
export ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="your-9router-dashboard-key"
export ANTHROPIC_MODEL="claude-with-fallback"
claude

Replace claude-with-fallback with your combo's name.

6Turn on RTK Token Saver

In the dashboard: Settings → RTK Token Saver → Enable. RTK compresses long tool outputs (file dumps, terminal logs, JSON) before they reach the model, saving about 20 to 40% of tokens depending on your work. Your source code is kept exactly; only the noise around it is compressed.

💡
For heavier compression, also enable Caveman mode. Together they can save around 65% on log-heavy sessions.

7Check the fallback works

  1. Use Claude Code normally until you near your 5-hour limit (the dashboard shows a countdown).
  2. Watch the current provider indicator.
  3. When the Claude limit runs out, it switches to your tier-2 provider (e.g. GLM 5.2).
  4. Keep coding: same interface, different engine, no new sign-in.

8Use it with other tools (optional)

  • Cursor: custom endpoint http://localhost:20128/v1 with your dashboard key.
  • Cline, Continue, RooCode or any OpenAI-compatible tool: base URL http://localhost:20128/v1.
  • Codex CLI:
Command · Route Codex through 9Router
export OPENAI_BASE_URL="http://localhost:20128/v1"
export OPENAI_API_KEY="your-9router-dashboard-key"

+Extra from Vaitis

  • Quality varies: backup models are cheaper but often weaker. For important changes, wait for your Claude limit to reset or review the backup's code carefully.
  • Compare: OmniRoute (guide 023) and FreeLLMAPI (guide 025) do similar routing; pick one rather than stacking all three.

title: Run a free image, video and lip-sync AI studio
summary: Open Generative AI is one open-source app that brings image, video and lip-sync generation across 200+ models into a single studio you can run in the browser, as a desktop app or on your own computer.
cost: The app is free; generation runs through Muapi and is pay-per-use (trial credits vary)
steps: Step 1: Choose how to run it
Step 2: Get and add your Muapi key
Step 4: Make a talking video from a photo
Step 5: Make a cinematic video from a photo
html:
✓What you need

  • Node.js 18 or newer and npm (only for self-hosting).
  • A Muapi.ai account for the API key. The app is free, but generation runs through Muapi and is paid per use.
  • macOS, Windows or Linux.
⚠️
Only use photos, voices and footage you have the right to use. Lip-sync turns a photo plus any voice into a talking video, so never use it to impersonate a real person.

1Choose how to run it

Path A: hosted web version (no install). Open muapi.ai/open-generative-ai, click Settings, paste your Muapi key (Step 2) and start.

Path B: desktop app. On the repository's Releases page download the .dmg (macOS), .exe (Windows) or .AppImage (Linux), install it and paste your key on first launch.

Path C: self-host. Clone the repository:

Command · Clone the repository
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/Anil-matcha/Open-Generative-AI.git
cd Open-Generative-AI

Set it up (plain npm install isn't enough; this builds the workspace packages first):

Command · Set up
npm run setup

Launch it and open http://localhost:3000:

Command · Launch
npm run dev
💡
The desktop app isn't signed, so macOS may say "cannot verify developer" (right-click → Open) and Windows SmartScreen may block it (More info → Run anyway). This is normal for small open-source projects.

2Get and add your Muapi key

  1. Sign up at muapi.ai.
  2. New accounts often get trial credits, but the amount varies, so check your balance before generating.
  3. Open API Keys → Create Key and copy it.
  4. Paste it when the app asks. It's stored in your browser's local storage and sent only to Muapi.

3Know the four studios

StudioWhat it does
Image StudioText-to-image and image-to-image across 50+ models (Flux, Midjourney, Ideogram, SDXL, Nano Banana 2, GPT-4o), with up to 14 reference images on supported models
Video StudioText-to-video and image-to-video (Sora 2, Veo 3, Kling v3, Wan 2.6, Seedance 2.0 and Pro, Hailuo 2.3, Runway Gen-3). Ratios 16:9, 9:16, 4:3, 3:4; usually 5, 10 or 15 seconds
Lip Sync StudioPortrait + audio → talking video, or video + audio → lip-synced video. Nine models across the two modes
Cinema StudioPreset camera, lens, focal length and aperture controls for when words alone don't give the look

4Make a talking video from a photo

  1. Open Lip Sync Studio and choose portrait + audio mode.
  2. Upload the photo.
  3. Upload or record audio in the voice you want (or create it with a text-to-speech tool).
  4. Choose a model: Infinite Talk I2V for realism or LatentSync for speed.
  5. Set aspect ratio and duration.
  6. Click Generate.

5Make a cinematic video from a photo

  1. Open Video Studio and choose image-to-video.
  2. Upload the photo.
  3. Add a prompt:
Prompt · Cinematic motion
Slow cinematic push-in, warm sunset light, film grain, shallow depth of field.
  1. Choose a high-quality model such as Seedance 2.0 Pro or Kling v3.
  2. Set 16:9 and 5 to 10 seconds.
  3. Click Generate.

+Extra from Vaitis

  • Control costs: test prompts on cheaper, shorter, lower-resolution runs; switch to premium models only for the final version.
  • Prompt formula for video: subject + action + camera movement + lighting + style (e.g. "a student opens a laptop, slow dolly-in, soft morning light, documentary style").
  • Label AI media in captions when you publish realistic AI video.

title: Run your coding tool on free and cheap AI with OmniRoute
summary: OmniRoute is a free local proxy that connects your coding tool to 200+ AI providers, sends each prompt to the cheapest option, falls back when one runs out and compresses prompts to save tokens.
cost: Free software; free provider tiers (which can change) and optional paid providers
steps: Step 3: Connect a few free providers
Step 4: Point your coding tool at OmniRoute
html:
✓What you need

  • Node.js 18 or newer and npm (or Docker).
  • A coding tool with a custom endpoint: Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Cline, Copilot, Windsurf, Continue or any OpenAI-compatible tool.
  • A browser for the dashboard.

1Install OmniRoute

npm is simplest:

Command · Install with npm
npm install -g omniroute

Or Docker:

Command · Run with Docker
docker run -p 20128:20128 diegosouzapw/omniroute

Or download the desktop app (Mac, Windows, Linux) from omniroute.online. Check the npm install:

Command · Check the version
omniroute --version

2Start it

Command · Launch OmniRoute
omniroute

It prints a dashboard address and an API endpoint, both on port 20128.

3Connect a few free providers

Open the dashboard, go to Providers and connect some free tiers:

Open in browser · DashboardOpen ↗
http://localhost:20128/dashboard
ProviderWhat you getHow to connect
iFlowKimi K2 Thinking, freeBrowser sign-in
QwenFree Qwen modelsBrowser sign-in
KiroFree Claude 4.5, GLM-5 and MiniMaxAWS Builder ID, Google or GitHub
NVIDIA NIMFree creditsSign up
GroqFast free tierAPI key
DeepSeekFree tokens at sign-upAPI key
GitHub CopilotFree tierGitHub sign-in

Click Connect on any of them; no credit card. Connect several and OmniRoute uses them all.

⚠️
Don't route Gemini CLI's free tokens through OmniRoute into other tools. Google's terms limit them to Gemini CLI itself, and using them elsewhere can get your account banned.

4Point your coding tool at OmniRoute

Create a key under Dashboard → Settings → API Keys. The base URL for every tool is http://localhost:20128/v1.

Claude Code:

Command · Route Claude Code
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="http://localhost:20128/v1"
export ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="your-dashboard-key"
claude

Cursor, Windsurf or Antigravity: set a custom endpoint to http://localhost:20128/v1 in Settings.

Codex CLI:

Command · Route Codex
export OPENAI_BASE_URL="http://localhost:20128/v1"
export OPENAI_API_KEY="your-dashboard-key"

Any other OpenAI-compatible tool: replace its openai.com base URL with http://localhost:20128/v1 and use your dashboard key.

5Build a routing combo

In Combos, build a chain. OmniRoute uses it in order and moves down when one runs out. Three starters:

  • free-only: free providers such as Gemini 3 Flash, Kimi K2 Thinking and Qwen3 Coder Plus. Costs $0 while you stay on free tiers.
  • maximize-Claude: your Claude Code subscription first, a cheap backup such as GLM 4.7 second, a free fallback such as Kimi K2 Thinking third.
  • always-on: a longer chain (Claude, a GPT Codex model, GLM, MiniMax, then a free model) so runs rarely stop.

Save it and use its alias (for example omniroute/free-only) as the model name in your tool.

💡
Providers set free tiers and can change or end them. Treat a $0 setup as a bonus, not a guarantee.

6Turn on compression

Settings → Compression, then pick a mode (fewer tokens for a little quality):

ModeApprox. savingsWhen to use
Off0%Debugging OmniRoute itself
Lite15%Safest
Standard30%Good default
Aggressive50%Long coding sessions
Ultra75%Maximum savings, some quality loss

+Extra from Vaitis

  • For learners on a budget: the free-only combo is enough to practise coding with an AI assistant without a paid plan.
  • Keep keys safe: your dashboard key controls paid providers too. Don't share it or put it in public code.

title: Turn one keyword into a finished short video
summary: MoneyPrinterTurbo is a free open-source pipeline that turns one keyword into a finished short video, with script, voiceover, subtitles, music and stock footage, through a simple web interface.
time: 15 to 30 minutes for first setup; a few minutes per video
cost: Free software; Pexels key is free; script AI is free (Ollama, g4f, Pollinations, ModelScope) or about a cent per video (DeepSeek, OpenAI)
steps: Step 5: Automate with the REST API (optional)
html:
✓What you need

  • Docker Desktop and Git. On Windows, set up WSL2 first.
  • A free Pexels API key (pexels.com/api) for stock footage.
  • An AI provider and key for the script. Free options: Ollama (local), g4f, Pollinations, ModelScope. Paid options (DeepSeek, OpenAI) cost about a cent per video.
  • 8 GB of RAM realistically. 4 GB only works with everything in the cloud; a local Ollama model needs 8 to 16 GB.
  • About 5 GB of free disk and 15 to 30 minutes for the first setup (the Docker image is about 3 GB).
⚠️
You need two keys, Pexels and an AI provider. "Set up in 10 seconds" is only the command time; the first real install takes 15 to 30 minutes, mostly the Docker download.

1Get your keys

Stock footage (free): sign up at pexels.com and copy the API key from your account.

Script AI: choose one lane:

LaneProvidersCostNotes
Free, cloudg4f, Pollinations, ModelScope$0Quality varies; can be unreliable
Free, localOllama$0Needs 8 to 16 GB RAM; installed separately
Paid, reliableOpenAI, DeepSeek, Moonshot, AIHubMixAbout $0.001 per 60-second videoBest scripts

For a first run, DeepSeek gives the best quality for the price (a few cents covers dozens of videos). For a strictly free path, Pollinations or g4f with Pexels footage gets you a finished video at $0.

2Download and configure

Command · Clone and copy the config
git clone https://github.com/harry0703/MoneyPrinterTurbo.git
cd MoneyPrinterTurbo
cp config.example.toml config.toml

On Windows use copy instead of cp. Open config.toml and fill in three things (use the provider block that matches your choice):

Config · config.toml
# 1. Stock footage
pexels_api_keys = ["YOUR_PEXELS_KEY_HERE"]

# 2. Which AI writes the script
llm_provider = "deepseek"   # or openai, moonshot, ollama, g4f, pollinations...

# 3. That provider's key and address (block name matches llm_provider)
[deepseek]
api_key = "YOUR_LLM_KEY_HERE"
base_url = "https://api.deepseek.com"
model_name = "deepseek-chat"

The file is well commented; each provider has its own block.

💡
Free local lane: set llm_provider = "ollama", then in the [ollama] block set base_url to http://host.docker.internal:11434/v1 and model_name to a model you've downloaded (for example llama3.1:8b). Run ollama list to check.

3Launch

Use the prebuilt image (faster):

Command · Launch (prebuilt image)
docker compose -f docker-compose.release.yml up

Or build locally (slower; only if you changed the code):

Command · Launch (build locally)
docker compose up

The first run downloads about 3 GB, so allow 10 to 20 minutes. Two services start:

  • Web interface: http://localhost:8501
  • REST API with docs: http://localhost:8080/docs
💡
Manage it with docker compose ps (see both containers), docker compose logs -f webui (watch logs) and docker compose down (stop and clean up).

4Make your first video

Open http://localhost:8501:

  1. Topic: one keyword or short phrase, e.g. "health", "morning routines" or "space facts".
  2. Language and ratio: English and 9:16 for Reels, Shorts and TikTok.
  3. Voice: start with en-US-AndrewNeural or any Edge TTS voice (free and natural).
  4. Subtitles: keep edge (fast, no GPU). Switch to whisper later if accuracy matters more than speed.
  5. Click Generate. You'll see each stage: script, search terms, footage download, voiceover, subtitles and the final FFmpeg encode.

The video is saved to storage/tasks/<task_id>/final-1.mp4.

💡
Chinese voices by default? The project's maintainer is Chinese; just pick an en-US voice. Empty video or no footage? Almost always the Pexels key (check storage/logs/), or the topic is too abstract; try a more concrete keyword.

5Automate with the REST API (optional)

API docs are at http://localhost:8080/docs. Every interface feature is an endpoint: submit a task, check its task_id, then download the MP4. Good for batch or scheduled runs.

⚠️
The output is a draft, not ready to publish. Stock footage relevance varies, and abstract topics pull odd clips, so always preview. Pexels and Pixabay are royalty-free for most uses, but check each clip's licence before commercial or large-scale publishing (task logs list the source links).

+Extra from Vaitis

  • Concrete topics work best: "5 Excel shortcuts", "what is SQL in 60 seconds", "3 free AI tools for students".
  • Add your brand: edit the final video in CapCut or Canva to add your logo and a call to action.
  • Batch a week: use the API to make 7 videos from 7 keywords in one go, then review and schedule them.

title: Get free AI for your apps and chatbots with FreeLLMAPI
summary: FreeLLMAPI combines the free tiers of 87 AI providers (1,313 free model endpoints) behind one OpenAI-compatible address, so your apps, coding tools and chatbots can use AI at no cost while you learn and prototype.
cost: Free (open source, MIT licence); optional $19 a year premium for the live model catalogue
steps: What it is and why it helps
Step 4: Use it from Python or any OpenAI tool
Step 5: Give your n8n chatbot a free AI brain
html:
✓What it is and why it helps

Most AI companies offer a small free tier: a few million tokens a month or a few thousand requests a day. One tier alone is a toy; added together they come to roughly 10.1 billion tokens a month across 87 providers and 736 model families. FreeLLMAPI stacks them behind one OpenAI-compatible endpoint:

  • A router picks the best available model for each request.
  • When a provider hits its rate limit, it falls over to the next one automatically.
  • It tracks usage per key so you stay under every free cap.
  • Your provider keys are stored encrypted.
  • It also speaks Anthropic's Messages API, so Claude-based tools can use it too.
⚠️
FreeLLMAPI's own disclaimer: it's for personal experimentation and learning, not production. Free tiers have no uptime guarantee and no top "frontier" models, speed varies, and quality dips late in the day as top models hit daily caps (they reset at UTC midnight). Before you serve real customers, switch to a paid API. Each provider's terms still apply when you route through it.

✓What you need

  • Docker Desktop (for the one-line or Compose install), or the desktop app for Windows or macOS.
  • Free accounts and API keys from a few AI providers (the dashboard lists them; Google Gemini, Groq and others offer free keys).
  • About 15 to 30 minutes.

1Install it

Option A: one line (Docker required). It creates ~/freellmapi, generates an encryption key, pulls the image and starts the container:

Command · One-line install
curl -fsSL https://freellmapi.co/install.sh | bash
💡
Prefer to read a script before running it? Open https://freellmapi.co/install.sh first. Re-running it is safe; your .env and encryption key are kept.

Option B: Docker Compose (Mac/Linux):

Command · Docker Compose install
git clone https://github.com/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi.git
cd freellmapi
ENCRYPTION_KEY="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
printf "ENCRYPTION_KEY=%s\nPORT=3001\n" "$ENCRYPTION_KEY" > .env
docker compose up -d

Option C: Windows. The easiest path is the .exe installer on the project's Releases page. There's also a macOS app, and mobile apps on Google Play and the App Store.

2Add your provider keys

  1. Open the dashboard:
Open in browser · DashboardOpen ↗
http://localhost:3001
  1. On the Keys page, add the free API keys you've collected.
  2. On Fallback Chain, drag providers into the order you prefer.
  3. Copy your unified API key from the top of the Keys page. This one key is what every app uses.

3Make your first request

Command · Test with curl
curl http://localhost:3001/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer freellmapi-your-unified-key" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "auto", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]}'

Every response includes an X-Routed-Via header showing which provider and model answered.

Choose how the router picks with the model field:

Model valueBehaviour
autoRouter decides (default blend)
auto:smartPrefers the most capable models
auto:fastPrefers the fastest responses
auto:reliablePrefers models with the best recent success rate
auto:balancedReliability first, then speed and capability
auto:<profile>Uses a named chain, e.g. auto:coding
a model idUses one specific model, e.g. gemini-2.5-flash

4Use it from Python or any OpenAI tool

Python · Python example
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:3001/v1", api_key="freellmapi-your-unified-key")
resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="auto",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Explain SQL joins in two sentences."}],
)
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)

Any tool with an "OpenAI base URL" setting works the same way: set it to http://localhost:3001/v1 and use your unified key. Claude-based tools point to http://localhost:3001 (they add /v1/messages themselves) with the same key.

5Give your n8n chatbot a free AI brain

This connects FreeLLMAPI to the SkillNavora WhatsApp workflow (whatsapp_ai_workflow.json):

  1. Open the Ask Grok node.
  2. Change the URL to http://<your-freellmapi-address>:3001/v1/chat/completions.
  3. In the body, change model: 'grok-4.7' to model: 'auto'.
  4. Edit its Header Auth credential: name Authorization, value Bearer freellmapi-your-unified-key.
💡
n8n must be able to reach FreeLLMAPI. If n8n runs on the same computer in Docker, use http://host.docker.internal:3001. n8n Cloud can't reach your laptop's localhost; run FreeLLMAPI on a server and only expose it securely (it's a single-user proxy, so never leave it open to the whole internet).

6Know the limits

  • No top frontier models, variable speed and no uptime guarantee.
  • Answers get weaker late in the UTC day as the best free models hit their caps, then reset at midnight UTC.
  • Free installs receive the model catalogue monthly; premium ($19 a year) gets new models the same day.
  • For anything customers depend on, move to a paid API.

+Troubleshooting

  • Forgot the server password? Click Forgot password?; the one-time code is printed in the server log (docker compose logs -f freellmapi) and lasts 15 minutes.
  • Dashboard won't load from another device? By default it only listens on 127.0.0.1. On a trusted home network only, start with HOST_BIND=0.0.0.0 docker compose up -d.
  • Update: docker compose pull && docker compose up -d (your data and .env are kept).
  • Uninstall: docker compose down -v, then delete the data folder.
